unit.why: A brief exemplum about an anonymous dead man who appears to his friends in a dream, quoted from the book of R. Yeiva within a homiletic section on the kavvanot of the commandments; it is not about a Hasidic figure.
unit.boundary_note: exemplum (marked ב) embedded in an ongoing homiletic discussion of kavvanot that begins in the previous division and continues in the next

stories.summary_en: A man appears to his friends in a dream and tells them that he is shamed in the next world: an angel proclaims the kavvanot with which he performed the commandments, and the righteous flee Paradise at hearing his folly and flaw. The moral drawn is that one should pray not to be shamed in the world to come.
